title: ISP: Interface Segregation
points: Prefer several small, focused interfaces over one fat one.
No class should be forced to implement methods it doesn't use.
trade: Too many tiny interfaces can scatter a concept. Group by the client's needs.
test: How does ISP relate to SRP and to LSP?
answer: ISP is SRP applied to interfaces. Fat interfaces also force empty or throwing implementations, which is how LSP violations start.

questions.question: RobotWorker implements Worker and leaves eat() empty. Which principle does the fix target?
options: ISP: split Worker into Workable and Eatable
questions.explanation: Interface Segregation: no class should be forced to implement methods it doesn't use.
